correctness.rationale: On the 2π-torus, Fourier normality gives an exact global lattice minimization. A Fibonacci witness yields \(O(a^{4/3})\); any global minimizer then has a small (<1/2) Diophantine residual and a nearest-integer frequency. An explicit unimodular Fibonacci basis establishes the best second-kind denominator lower bound and domination term by term, yielding eventual exact Fibonacci-mode minimization. Binet's formula and uniform exclusion of far j prove the log-periodic envelope for all large a; the two-branch crossing proves nonconstant exact extrema and all subsequential values. Numerical finite checks are explicitly supplementary, not the proof.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 probability paper explicitly treats this irrational torus drift only qualitatively. The natural golden ratio is a canonical extremal badly approximable slope; the exact finite-parameter mode selection, sharp power, nonconstant log-periodic envelope, and two distinct limiting constants resolve a concrete question of how strongly averaged relaxation improves. The absence of one universal normalized gap constant is qualitative structure, rather than a routine numerical coefficient. The consequence for averaged relaxation is carefully limited to order, preventing a false extension.
